meta.topic: Where You End and Others Begin

headline: Boundaries define where you end and others begin—the lines that protect your wellbeing
universal_truth: Healthy relationships require healthy boundaries; knowing your limits enables genuine connection
fun_facts: People with clear boundaries report higher relationship satisfaction
Boundaries aren't walls—they're gates you control; you decide what enters and leaves
Many boundary violations happen through gradual erosion, not dramatic crossing
discussion_questions: Where are your boundaries clear and where are they fuzzy?
What happens when you don't maintain your limits?
How do you communicate boundaries without damaging relationships?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Where does your responsibility end and someone else's begin? What are you willing to accept and what crosses a line? Boundaries are the edges of you—defining what's yours to give and what's yours to protect.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Boundaries can feel selfish. But without them, we burn out, resent, and lose ourselves. Why are boundaries essential?

options.text: Boundaries protect wellbeing and enable authentic connection—without limits, you give until depleted and connect without knowing who you are; boundaries make real relationships possible
options.response: Yes. Resentment grows where boundaries don't exist. Burnout follows boundaryless giving. Knowing where you end lets you give freely from a protected core.
They can, but healthy boundaries are gates, not walls—you control access rather than eliminating it...

q1.title: Types of Boundaries
q1.script: Boundaries exist in many domains: physical, emotional, time, energy, information. Each requires different limits. Knowing your boundaries in each area creates comprehensive protection.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Types of Boundaries"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Communicating Limits
q2.script: Boundaries work when communicated. Unexpressed limits get crossed innocently. Clear, calm communication of what you need protects you without attacking others.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Enforcement Required
q3.script: Stated boundaries that aren't enforced become suggestions. Consistent enforcement teaches others that your limits are real. Without follow-through, boundaries erode.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Healthy relationships require healthy boundaries. Knowing your limits enables genuine connection. Define where you end.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 321. Tomorrow, we'll explore what's yours to share—privacy. Until then, notice where your boundaries are clear and where they're fuzzy.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Boundary Mapping - Where Are Your Edges?
growTrack.activity: Map your boundaries in key areas: time, energy, physical space, emotional sharing, information. Where are they firm? Where are they porous? What boundary, if strengthened, would most improve your wellbeing?
